Nike sales recovery pushed back as Bank of America cuts earnings forecast Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America has cut its Nike Inc (NYSE:NKE, XETRA:NKE) earnings forecasts after pushing back its expected sales recovery, warning that the sportswear group faces prolonged challenges in rebuilding growth.

The broker now expects Nike's sales to inflect in the third quarter of financial 2028, rather than the second quarter previously forecast, reflecting a longer period of weakness in its Jordan business.

Bank of America reduced its financial 2028 earnings per share estimate by 11% to $1.31, as Nike works with retailers to manage lower Jordan volumes.

The approach is expected to spread the decline in sales over a longer period rather than allowing retailers to absorb a sharp reduction in orders at once.

Despite the lower earnings forecast, Bank of America maintained its $24 price target, increasing the valuation multiple applied to its financial 2028 earnings estimate to 18 times from 16 times.

The change reflects a recent expansion in valuation multiples across Nike's industry peers, although the broker retained its Underperform rating.

Bank of America sees risks to both market consensus earnings forecasts and the 30 times earnings multiple currently implied by broader expectations.

Nike's forthcoming investor day will be important in assessing whether its innovation pipeline can accelerate the recovery, particularly across performance and lifestyle products.

However, the broker cautioned that new product launches alone would not guarantee stronger growth, with consumer response ultimately determining the pace and scale of any turnaround.

The longer-term sales outlook also faces a challenging starting point, with management expected to provide a growth framework potentially extending to financial 2031.

Bank of America estimates that sales could decline 9% in financial 2028, fall a further 1% in financial 2029 and then grow 4% annually over the following three years.

That trajectory would leave revenue broadly flat against financial 2026 levels of $46 billion by financial 2031.

Margins and the allocation of cost savings will also be central to the recovery.

Nike's PACE programme targets $2.5 billion in gross cost savings by financial 2031, with most benefits expected in the later years and spread across gross margin and selling, general and administrative expenses.

Bank of America estimates that a 9% operating margin in financial 2031 would support earnings per share of $2.15, rising to $2.40 at a 10% margin.

The broker also questioned the sustainability of Nike's dividend, with its payout ratio forecast at 145% in financial 2027 and 125% in financial 2028.

It models more than 90% of free cash flow being used to fund the dividend, leaving limited financial flexibility while earnings remain under pressure.

Will Morgan Stanley's Vinyl Equity Deal Fuel Wealth Management Growth?

Trading disclosure

Morgan Stanley MS continues to expand its wealth management and workplace financial solutions businesses through strategic acquisitions. The company has announced an agreement to acquire Vinyl Equity, a digital-first, SEC-registered transfer agent and shareholder recordkeeping platform.

Founded in 2022, Vinyl Equity provides digital workflows, real-time reporting and streamlined shareholder administration, with a focus on complex private-company transactions, including initial public offerings (IPOs). The deal will expand Morgan Stanley at Work's capabilities by integrating cap table management, equity administration, share transfer and wealth management infrastructure across private and public markets.

The combined platform will connect companies' equity management needs with Morgan Stanley's wealth management services, helping deepen relationships with corporate clients, founders, executives and shareholders. The deal will also strengthen the company's infrastructure for potential future tokenization initiatives as blockchain technology and digital ownership solutions gain traction.

Morgan Stanley expects to close the transaction in the first quarter of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions. The deal's financial terms were not disclosed.

Will Morgan Stanley's Acquisition Strategy Drive Growth?

Morgan Stanley's acquisition of Vinyl Equity supports its broader strategy of reducing reliance on capital markets by expanding its wealth and investment management businesses. Over the years, acquisitions, including Eaton Vance, ETRADE Financial, Shareworks and EquityZen, have broadened its offerings across advisor-led, self-directed and workplace channels, helping diversify its revenue mix. As a result, the aggregate contribution of its Wealth and Investment Management businesses to total net revenues increased to nearly 54% in 2025 from 26% in 2010.

Morgan Stanley is also expanding its digital asset offerings through Ethereum and Solana ETPs and ETRADE's launch of spot digital asset trading. This will likely further strengthen its wealth management ecosystem.

The Vinyl Equity deal is expected to build on this momentum by enhancing Morgan Stanley at Work's workplace financial solutions platform. The platform serves more than 3,400 corporate clients and supports 6.7 million participants, covering roughly 50% of the S&P 500 and more than 70% of the top 100 unicorns by market capitalization. By adding transfer agency capabilities, the acquisition will enable Morgan Stanley to better serve companies and shareholders across private and public markets, strengthen its competitive positioning and create cross-selling opportunities across its corporate and individual client base.

AST SpaceMobile Sinks 8% on Q3 Miss as BofA Slashes Target to $45 Over Rocket Risk ©@3DSculptor from Getty Images via Canva, @metamorworks from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

AST SpaceMobile fell 8% today on a third-quarter miss and BofA's price target cut to $45 from $80.

Revenue nearly tripled to $42.3 million, but BofA is worried about launches and AST's plan to build its own rocket.

AST's goal of about 45 satellites in orbit has slipped to mid-2027, and its next three are waiting on a SpaceX launch date.

Rocket Lab's new rocket has slipped too, and AT&T is waiting on AST's U.S. service.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS:NASDAQ) is down 8% today on a third-quarter miss, a day after its Rakuten joint venture sent shares soaring. BofA cut its price target to $45 from $80, warning that launches could slip and that building its own rocket adds risk.

That reaches SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ), AST's launcher and rival; Rocket Lab (RKLB:NASDAQ), which is building a rocket of its own; and AT&T (T:NYSE), which is waiting on AST's U.S. service.

Costs ran ahead of sales

Revenue came in at $42.3 million, up from $14.7 million a year earlier. The miss came on costs: adjusted operating expenses rose $14.5 million from the second quarter to $133.6 million. Analysts went into the report expecting revenue to reach $609 million in 2027:

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

And the 2027 estimate depends on satellites that aren't in orbit yet.

Launches are still the whole story

AST's goal of about 45 BlueBirds in orbit has slipped to mid-2027 from early 2027, and 12 are up today. BlueBirds 14 to 16 are still waiting on a launch date from SpaceX, which flew 12 launches for customers in the third quarter, down from 15 a year earlier, and has agreed to buy spectrum for its own phone service.

So I get why AST wants Blacklift, its own reusable rocket due in late 2028. Rocket Lab shows the catch: it posted record third-quarter revenue of $268 million, but its Neutron rocket won't fly before 2027.

For AT&T, the year-end date matters more than the rocket. Its postpaid phone churn held at 0.92% in the third quarter, and satellite coverage would give its customers one more reason to stay as SpaceX moves into phone service.

title: Vanguard Inks $4B of Private Debt for Altruist Deal

Vanguard Inks $4B of Private Debt for Altruist Deal

Trading disclosure

You can find original article here WealthManagement. Subscribe to our free daily WealthManagement newsletters.

(Bloomberg) -- Vanguard Group has raised about $4 billion of private debt to finance its acquisition of digital wealth platform Altruist.

The firm, the second largest asset manager globally, borrowed in the private placement bond market, according to people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified as the details are confidential. Companies tap that market to source funds directly from institutional investors like life insurers.

Bank of America Corp., Citigroup Inc. and JPMorgan Chase & Co. arranged the transaction, some of the people said.

Representatives for Vanguard, Citi and JPMorgan declined to comment. A representative for Bank of America did not respond to a request for comment.

Vanguard, which oversees about $13.3 trillion in global assets as of July 31, has been ramping up its efforts to expand into wealth management. It announced plans to purchase Altruist in August after making an initial investment in 2020.

Altruist provides technology that helps independent financial advisers manage their clients' money and run their businesses in one place. It once branded itself as a "modern custodian," offering advisers an alternative platform in a market where incumbents like Fidelity Investments and Charles Schwab Corp. dominate.

Jack Bogle-founded Vanguard is one of the latest companies to raise debt in the private placement market, following deals from the National Football League and Chick-fil-A Inc. earlier this year.

Going the private placement route is an option for companies looking for privacy and flexibility, as it doesn't typically require the same securities filings for public debt sales.

title: Bank of America Drops Nvidia From Elite Stock List. Coincidence or Jensen Huang Fallout?
detail:
Bank of America Drops Nvidia From Elite Stock List. Coincidence or Jensen Huang Fallout?

Tue, November 10, 2026 at 5:56 AM MST 2 min read

BAC

LRCX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America has pulled Nvidia from its US 1 List, the bank's short roster of best stock ideas. The cut came days after CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a woman US intelligence reportedly suspected of spying for China.

The bank declined to explain. Nvidia keeps its Buy rating. However, the chipmaker sits in most US index funds, so its slide reaches ordinary savers, not just traders.

Did Bank of America Punish Nvidia Over the Huang Scandal?

Nvidia did not leave alone. Bank of America also dropped Micron, a memory chip maker, and Lam Research, which builds chipmaking machines. Neither company has any tie to Huang.

All three keep their Buy ratings.

The three stocks also moved in opposite directions Monday. Nvidia fell more than 4% as its board probed Huang, while Micron and Lam Research climbed.

So the bank cut one scandal-hit stock and two rising ones in the same move. No research note explaining it was released, ROIC reported.

Nvidia (NVDA), Micron (MU), and Lam Research (LRCX) share price moves, November 9–10, 2026, Source: TradingView
What Does Losing a Top-Pick Slot Mean for Nvidia Shareholders?

A Buy rating means the bank expects the stock to rise. A US 1 slot marks one of its strongest convictions. Nvidia lost the latter.

The bank has reshuffled this way before. In February, it added Lam to the list and removed AMD, which kept its Buy rating.

Elsewhere on Wall Street, Bernstein reaffirmed its outperform rating on Nvidia on November 9.

Meanwhile, Nvidia entered a bear market Monday, trading about 26% below its October record.

Bank of America's chip analyst, Vivek Arya, has tied the sector's gains to artificial intelligence (AI) spending.

"We continue to view AI/data center to drive the majority of gains."

Huang faces a November 11 deadline to tell Congress whether he will brief lawmakers. Nvidia reports earnings on November 17, a day before the proposed closed-door briefing.

Nvidia now holds a split verdict from Bank of America. The bank still rates it a Buy. It just no longer ranks it among its best ideas.

BofA highlighted upcoming satellite launches, a potential commercial agreement with T-Mobile and additional sovereign satellite deals as possible catalysts for AST SpaceMobile, according to Investing.com.

Five out of 13 analysts covering the stock rate it 'Buy' or 'Strong Buy,' while six rate it 'Hold' and two rate the stock 'Sell' or 'Strong Sell,' according to Koyfin.

AST SpaceMobile reported third-quarter revenue of $42.3 million, below analyst estimates of around $46 million, on Monday, but maintained its 2026 revenue outlook of $150 million to $200 million.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) shares drew investor attention on Tuesday after BofA Securities sharply cut its price target on the satellite company, citing slower launches and delays to commercial availability.

BofA lowered its price target to $45 from $80 while maintaining a 'Neutral' rating on the shares, according to The Fly. This implies around 22% upside from AST SpaceMobile's previous closing price of $36.89.

ASTS shares traded 3.4% lower in premarket trading at the time of writing.

Five out of 13 analysts covering the stock rate it 'Buy' or 'Strong Buy,' while six rate it 'Hold' and two rate the stock 'Sell' or 'Strong Sell,' according to Koyfin. Their 12-month price target ranges from $42.50 to $108, with an average of $74.68.

BofA Flags Satellite Launch And Commercialization Risks

BofA updated its model following AST SpaceMobile's third-quarter results and management commentary, citing a slower launch cadence and later commercial availability as reasons for the reduced price target, The Fly reported.

The firm also highlighted three areas of concern: satellite launch cadence, the timing of commercial availability, and technology execution risks associated with the company's plans to develop its own launch vehicles using Firefly Aerospace's Miranda engine, according to a report published by Investing.com.

AST SpaceMobile is targeting 45 satellites in orbit by mid-2027. However, the timeline could slip depending on launch vehicle availability. Reaching this milestone is important to the company's commercial service timeline and potential time-to-market advantage, Investing.com reported.

Separately, on its third-quarter earnings call, management said it was targeting initial intermittent nationwide service activation by the end of 2026, followed by consumer beta trials in early 2027. The company said it would need about 45 to 60 BlueBird satellites to enable continuous service in key markets.
